This comparison outlines the specific Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification codes that define Koder for direkte orale antikoagulantia (DOAC) for the purpose of healthcare quality measurement. According to the 2023 data, these codes are utilized to track and evaluate the quality of treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation [^src1]. 

The framework identifies four distinct drug codes within this category. These include [[b01ae07|B01AE07]] for dabigatran, [[b01af01|B01AF01]] for rivaroxaban, [[b01af02|B01AF02]] for apixaban, and [[b01af03|B01AF03]] for edoxaban [^src1]. Because the available evidence consists of a single dated section from 2023, it is not possible to identify trends, improvements, or declines in the usage or classification of these medications over time. The list serves strictly as a definitional baseline for which pharmacological agents are included when calculating clinical quality indicators for atrial fibrillation management [^src1].
